Subject: Unexpected slowdowns on dedicated pool this morning

Hi Mina,

We saw a sharp increase in tail latencies across our inference endpoints in US-west this morning between ~02:45-03:30 PT. Traffic pattern didn't change on our side — we ran replay tests. The drop impacted three mission-critical routes and caused a partial degradation in customer UX.

Can you share what you have so far (root cause, timeline, evidence) and confirm whether we are eligible for an SLA credit? Marco in procurement is copied for billing follow-up.

Thanks,
Elena

Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected slowdowns on dedicated pool this morning

Elena — thanks for the heads up and I'm sorry for the disruption. We opened an ops incident (OPS-4589) and our SREs are triaging. Preliminary notes:

- Symptoms: increased p95/p99 token latencies and queuing on Novarc's dedicated tenant between 02:42–03:28 PT. No model changes from your side.
- Early signal: allocator imbalance and node fragmentation in the us-west dedicated pool; several nodes entered a transient warmup state and did not accept normal fairshare assignments.
- Immediate action: SREs applied a targeted allocator rebalance and forced warmup drain at 03:10 PT which reduced tail latency by ~70% by 03:22 PT.

I'll put together an evidence packet (scheduler traces, allocator logs, KV cache hit rates, timeline) and a proposed SLA bridge/credit calculation for review. In parallel Ben and Camila will work with you on any billing terms.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to go over the packet and next steps?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Unexpected slowdowns on dedicated pool this morning

Looping in some initial analysis — I pulled allocator traces and node-level metrics. Early root cause hypothesis: a tag-mismatch in autoscaler rollout (deploy 20261214-03) caused a subset of reserved nodes to be marked as unavailable for fairshare assignment, producing temporary overconsolidation on remaining nodes and increased queue depth.

Planned next steps:
- Produce evidence bundle (allocator_trace_20261220.tar.gz, kvcache_metrics_20261220.csv) — Camila to assemble.
- Calculate credit using our SLA policy baseline (Ben) and draft the SLA bridge term sheet (attached).
- Ops follow-up: small hotfix to autoscaler tagging and an automated post-roll validation to prevent recurrence (Sojin).

Mina — recommend we propose a provisional credit and schedule a joint review before any final billing adjustments.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Evidence bundle and provisional credit calculation

Elena / team — attached is the evidence bundle we discussed and a provisional credit calc. Quick notes:

- What’s attached: allocator_trace_20261220.tar.gz (scheduler traces, per-node allocation timeline), kvcache_metrics_20261220.csv (prefix/KV cache hit rates by route), credit_calculation_novarc.xlsx, sla_bridge_term-sheet.pdf
- Key findings: allocator trace shows a 14-minute window where three reserved nodes failed to advertise fairshare availability due to a tagging race during autoscaler rollout. KV cache hit-rates dropped ~12% for affected routes during that window; we estimate effective throughput reduction in the impacted shard of ~35%.
- Proposed credit: provisional credit equals 6.5% of December committed monthly spend (see spreadsheet) — offered as an SLA bridge while we complete the post-incident validation.

Requesting: a short meeting for Friday 12/17 at 10:00 PT to review the packet and agree the next steps for formal credit and a technical postmortem.

Camila Reyes
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: corrective actions, timeline, and rollforward commitments

Elena / Marco / team — thank you for the call and the constructive review. This message captures agreed items and commit dates:

1) Root cause recap (confirmed)
- Autoscaler rollout tag race (deploy 20261214-03) caused transient node unavailability for fairshare assignment; result was allocator fragmentation and queue build on remaining nodes for ~14 minutes.

2) Permanent fixes (in progress / scheduled)
- Autoscaler hotfix (Sojin): avoid tag race by serializing tag publish; rollout scheduled 2026-12-21 02:00 PT, validation window 1 hour.
- Post-roll validation (Sojin & Ops): automated fairness check within 5 minutes of any autoscaler deployment.
- Allocator monitoring improvement (Camila): new alert for sustained per-tenant allocation skew > 8% for > 5 minutes. Delivery: 2027-01-05.

3) Customer commitments
- Provisional SLA bridge credit: Redwood to apply a 6.5% credit to Dec invoice upon agreement; final amount subject to audit of logs (we agreed to finalize by 2026-12-28).
- Evidence package delivered (links above & attachments).
- War room notes and full post-incident writeup to follow (target: 2026-12-28).

4) Owners & contacts
- Mina: customer comms & credit coordination
- Ben: commercial reconciliation
- Camila: evidence package & technical writeup
- Sojin: fixes, rollout, and validation

5) Next steps
- Redwood to confirm hotfix rollout start by 12/21 02:00 PT and report progress to Novarc ops channel.
- Final postmortem and credit calculation by 12/28.
- Optional follow-up review (30 min) the week of 1/4 to discuss long-term mitigations.

If that aligns with Novarc's expectations we'll proceed. Thanks again for the partnership here — we know incidents like this are disruptive and appreciate the collaboration to close the loop.

Best,
